scope: Proposition 3.1 (Uniform local compiler) of the manuscript “An explicit power saving for the exact discrete Fourier transform” (preprints/An-explicit-power-saving-for-the-exact-discrete-Fourier-transform-September-25-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 130 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 670d0115ea2553e6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let r ≥ 1 and let u be any primitive rth root of unity. The matrix Fr(u) = (uij)0≤i,j<r has a word on exactly r coordinates with O(1 + log4 r) slots, each of which is either 1. a monomial layer, or 2. disjoint copies of C on ordered pairs, with identity on every remaining singleton. There is one fixed repeating pattern of slot types into which all these words can be padded. For any finite collection of widths at most R, the words can therefore be synchronized in O(1 + log4 R) slots. Their schedules and scalar coefficients can be prepared in time rO(1), with an absolute exponent, counting both exact scalar arithmetic and integer bookkeeping. Besides u and the fixed constant i, this preparation needs only power-of-two roots of orders at most 8r. Coefficients are specified by shared arithmetic programs over these roots and rational numbers. Every division is by a proved nonzero scalar; every structural choice uses integers alone. Neither a test for zero of a complex number nor conjugation of input data is required.
